Label claim: generates 8 PPM of hydrogen per tablet. Ingredients (product page, 2026-03): molecular hydrogen (H2), magnesium blend, citric acid, mineral support complex. [MISSING] amounts per tablet.
product.ingredient_visual: a clear glass of water with a white tablet fizzing at the bottom and fine hydrogen bubbles rising; the water stays clear and clean. Never cloudy, coloured or foamy. [TO CONFIRM]

avatar._note: Edenvia sells one product to MANY avatars, one per angle. Each angle has a full sheet in edenvia/avatars/*.md (identity, pain, failed solutions, trigger, verbatim language, root-cause bridge, big idea, hooks). The block below is the DEFAULT angle A1 only; the spec of every ad names its angle and takes the avatar from that angle's sheet.
avatar.who: Default angle is A5 blood sugar (first test, founder 2026-10-11): a man in his 40s or older who has progressively surrendered foods he loves because carb-heavy meals leave him drained, crashing and afraid of losing the rest of his day; middle-aged, soft build, family man; food is a visual character (pizza, pancakes, syrup, diner breakfast). Full sheet: edenvia/avatars/blood-sugar-avatar.md. Never a young fitness model.

secondary_problems: foods he gave up: pizza, pancakes, family breakfasts, dinners out
organizing life around what he can no longer tolerate

a nap he never used to need after lunch

cinnamon, berberine, chromium, generic 'blood sugar' supplements

the whole family at the same table eating the same thing

mechanism: plain words: a workout (or just a day) creates oxidative stress; when the body can't clear it, the inflammatory response stays switched on and recovery never finishes — that is the morning stiffness. The tablet turns a glass of water into hydrogen-rich water; hydrogen is the smallest molecule there is, so it reaches the cells where the oxidative stress sits and helps the body switch the response back off. Structure/function wording only ('helps support', 'helps maintain'). Jargon never printed: selective antioxidant, hydroxyl radical, reactive oxygen species, endothelial, redox, NSAID, bioavailability. Allowed because the brand itself prints them: 'inflammation', 'inflammatory response', 'oxidative stress', 'cellular', '8PPM'.

banned.\\b(treat|treats|treating|cure|cures|cur: compliance (DSHEA): no disease treatment / cure / prevention claim
banned.\\b(arthritis|GERD|fibromyalgia|neuropat: compliance: never name a disease or medical condition
banned.\\b(FDA[- ]approved|clinically proven|cl: compliance: no clinical-proof or FDA claim (site says 'clinically inspired', never 'proven')
banned.\\b(replaces? (your )?(PPIs?|antacids?|p: compliance: never say it replaces a medication (phone KB §5)
banned.\\b(capsule|capsules|gel ?cap|pill|pills: C2: the product is an effervescent tablet, never a capsule / pill / powder
banned.\\bDr\\. [A-Z][a-z]+|\\bPhD\\b|\\bcelebr: compliance: never an invented NAMED doctor, title or celebrity. 'Trusted by healthcare professionals' and unnamed 'doctors' are allowed (founder, hardcore marketing).
banned.\\b(A1C|HbA1c|insulin resistance|diabete: compliance (DSHEA): the swipe file (Metabolae/Lirae) prints these; Edenvia does not — disease, drug and lab-marker names never in an Edenvia ad. Say 'blood sugar', 'post-meal crash', 'your numbers'.

compliance: Structure/function claims only: 'supports', 'helps maintain', 'may support', 'helps your body…'. Never diagnose, treat, cure, prevent, reverse, heal, manage a condition (DSHEA rollout doc, 2026-09-21).

Never name a disease or medical condition in headline or body. 'Inflammation', 'oxidative stress', 'stiff joints', 'afternoon crash', 'stubborn numbers' are allowed; 'arthritis', 'hypertension', 'diabetes', 'fatty liver' are not.
No invented NAMED doctors or celebrities. 'Trusted by healthcare professionals' is allowed (founder, 2026-10-11).
No fake testimonials as real; no stat without a real source and its footnote (B16).
No body before/after presented as a real customer.
Never say it replaces a medication or that someone should stop one.

Disclaimer (short DSHEA version), only where the template has the slot: 'These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.'
Tone: the founder wants VERY AGGRESSIVE ads (2026-10-11). Aggressive on the pain, the enemy belief and the offer; never aggressive on a disease claim.
'*Results may vary' footnote allowed wherever the template carries one (follow the swipe file).
Age callouts ('after 40', 'over 50') allowed when the template carries one (follow the swipe file).

The swipe-file brands (Metabolae, Lirae) print A1C, insulin, diabetes, metformin, dialysis. Edenvia clones the template, not the disease claim: every such line is rewritten to structure/function before the spec passes lint.
